summary: 1. Total production beat target every day (+2.7% to +12.8%), and ore resumed Sep 18 (1,116 BCM, ending a three-day zero-ore run) but then missed its own daily target by 46-88% on each of the following three days (Sep 19 -71.9%, Sep 20 -45.5%, Sep 21 -78.5%). 2. MTD total surplus held in a narrow +6.9% to +7.1% band across all four days; MTD ore surplus kept narrowing (37.1% down to 25.3%) purely on the target-base effect, since the ore total itself barely moved. 2. 3. EX-253's fault, open since 16-Sep and carried across four prior passes as an unconfirmed theory, is now root-caused in writing: a swing motor and swing gearbox failure with three broken slew-gear teeth. 4. A 21-Sep maintenance email (Louw Weideman to Joe Coleman) puts the replacement slew gear and bearing's in-country arrival at 08-Oct-2026, plus 3-5 days customs clearance before release to site — meaning the unit will run at least three weeks down from this point, a materially longer repair than the original 49-day saga's single-fault window. 5. The same email confirms DT-128's parallel fault (down since 18-Sep) as a cylinder-head problem mixing coolant with engine oil at 34,892 hours, with a replacement engine already in stock and the swap under way. 3. 6. Drilling swung from a beat (Sep 18, +13.95%) to a complete zero-meter shutdown (Sep 21, -100%, avail 100%/util 0%) as two blasts fired on consecutive days (Sep 20, Sep 21) and drew drilling stock down from 23,358 BCM to 3,268 BCM. 7. A Sep 19 pit-constraint meeting had already flagged blocks 513/514 depleting in 2-3 days — faster than a 5-day field estimate — two days ahead of the Sep 21 shutdown, and the Sep 21 shift meeting logs 65.5 cumulative standby hours pending an unresolved decision on shutting down Stage 4 versus scaling back the wall. 8. Survey reconciliation flipped positive for the first time in over a week: Sep 19 (+10.07%) and Sep 20 (+4.11%) narrowed the cumulative MTD gap from -11.49% to -9.69%, with the monthly target now 84.05% achieved and 4 days left in the fiscal cycle. 9. See [[survey-volume-reconciliation]]. A new Saudi National Day blasting restriction is now active: the new magazine manager (Hamid) is limiting police escorts to one trip per blast and capping loads to roughly 32-35 t, forcing a split-location workaround — a direct constraint on blast cadence for the rest of the month. See [[blasting-and-drilling]]. The Sep 21 monthly production and spatial-compliance review reports September actual production roughly 411K t short of the original 1.8M t quarterly forecast, with spatial compliance at 87% tonnage / 72% area, both below the 85% goal. Peter set a stretch target of >1.6M t by month-end. A fatigue-reporting trust gap surfaced at the 20-Sep weekly HSE meeting (operators fear job/badge loss for honest self-reporting) alongside a strong YTD lagging-indicator record (769,363 man-hours, zero LTIs since Mar 2023). A haul truck entered the pit at 8% fuel (20-Sep) and DT-243 ran out of fuel entirely the next day, with a standing instruction not to report fuel shortages on the group chat overruled in real time. See [[safety-inspection-patterns]]. Two open dust-suppression pump faults surfaced at the same HSE meeting and the following day's Stage 4/5 planning meeting — one traced to a supplier (Jamil) that has not serviced the unit since 12-Aug, a second to chemical wear on a different pump — alongside an open EX-123 fire-suppression fault with ZAID technicians due the following week. No new source material has landed since roughly Sep 21 4 PM (checked against current file mtimes) — this is a backlog catch-up, not a same-day pass. No content removed or renamed from RAW.
